items.title: Set up elevated access for Gustav
items.detail: Create dedicated admin account or configure passwordless sudo for specific trusted commands (tailscaled, gateway restarts etc.) so Gustav can run elevated commands without Aaron's personal password being sent over Telegram.

items.title: Weekly Sonnet diagnostic + monthly Opus strategic review
items.detail: Weekly cron (Sonnet): routine system health check — crons, memory, scripts, configs. Monthly cron (Opus): strategic audit — is the architecture right, what's being wasted, what should change. Post results to #diagnostics.

items.title: Push Mission Control repo to GitHub Pages origin
items.detail: Local `mission-control` repo is clean but remains hundreds of commits ahead of `origin/main`, so GitHub Pages is still stale and still showing the old April-era site. Needs an explicit push to publish the current dashboard. This is now a pure approval blocker: Aaron needs to confirm whether I should push the current local state to `origin/main` and refresh the public site.

items.title: Add Buffer smoke-test / queue-health logging
items.detail: Structured Buffer health evidence exists via `automation/buffer-health-check.js`, and the daily diagnostic now explicitly refreshes that evidence first so checks use same-day queue/login data plus a fresh screenshot. Next improvement, if wanted, would be splitting this into a dedicated scheduled preflight instead of relying on the diagnostic job itself.

items.title: Investigate gateway reconnect 1005 noise
items.detail: Investigation complete: the repeated `Max reconnect attempts (0) reached after code 1005` errors are being triggered by the Discord channel health monitor, which marks `discord:default` as `stale-socket` after ~30 minutes without events and restarts it roughly every 35 minutes. The gateway and provider recover cleanly within seconds after each restart, so this currently looks like restart-path noise on an idle Discord connection rather than a sustained outage. If we want to suppress the noise, the next clean fix is either disabling `channels.discord.healthMonitor.enabled` for this low-traffic deployment or increasing the stale-event threshold.

items.title: Resolve Altair Codex runtime failure on real runs
items.detail: Resolved on 21 May: reran the real Lyra foundation task through the current Altair Codex runner, confirmed the old exit-status-2 failure report was stale, and captured a successful result packet at `altair/reports/lyra-foundation-v1-result.json`. The run produced a new `lyra/` foundation with a structured brief schema, SKC brand/config skeleton, template placeholders for poster/leaflet/social/document assets, QA scaffold, and top-level documentation. Next logical step, if wanted, is a narrow brief-to-template assembly path for one asset type such as `poster-a4`.

items.title: Build first Lyra brief-to-template assembly path
items.detail: Completed on 22 May: Lyra now has a first working `poster-a4` brief-to-template assembly path. `lyra/pipeline/assemble_poster_a4.py` validates a poster brief plus the SKC brand profile, reads named slots from the poster template, maps factual/copy/visual content into a deterministic intermediate package, and writes both JSON + Markdown review artifacts under `lyra/outputs/<brief_id>/`. Example input exists at `lyra/briefs/examples/poster-a4-sunday-beginners.json`, and validation was rerun successfully via the assembler plus `python3 -m py_compile`. Remaining blockers are intentional: no final renderer yet, and brand logo/colour/font values are still TBD in the brand skeleton.

items.title: Build first Lyra poster render step
items.detail: Completed on 22 May: Lyra now has a first working `poster-a4` render step layered on top of the existing brief-to-template assembly flow. The pipeline can take the Sunday beginners example brief plus the SKC working brand pack and produce real output artifacts: `lyra/outputs/poster-a4-sunday-beginners/poster-a4.png`, `poster-a4-print.pdf`, `render-manifest.json`, alongside the assembled package. This is Lyra's own first premium-modern yellow/black pass with deterministic text placement rather than AI-baked poster text. Remaining intentional gaps: no leaflet/social/document renderers yet, and brand refinements can still improve the creative direction after Aaron review.

items.title: Refine Lyra poster style to v2
items.detail: Completed on 22 May: Lyra's first poster render was refined after Aaron's review. The v2 pass keeps the premium modern yellow/black direction but improves typography consistency, adds stronger graphic treatment, clearer sectioning, and a more promotional composition for the Sunday beginners example output.

items.title: Add supplied-image insertion to Lyra poster pipeline
items.detail: Completed on 22 May: Lyra can now accept a supplied portrait/hero image for poster-a4 briefs via source_materials, route it into the hero slot, and render clean poster outputs. Normal photos use cover-crop; transparent PNGs preserve alpha and use contained placement. Example brief and outputs were added for the supplied-image path.

items.title: Build Lyra lead-gen poster mode
items.detail: Completed on 22 May: Lyra now has a real reusable `lead-gen` poster-a4 mode. Briefs can explicitly set `template_mode: "lead-gen"`, the schema/pipeline validate it, and the Sunday beginners plus supplied-image examples render intentionally through that path for acquisition/free-trial style posters.

items.title: Build Altair v2 true-agent foundation
items.detail: Completed on 22 May: Altair now has its first true-agent local foundation. Added identity/autonomy/escalation docs, a real inbox with lifecycle states, task-state schema, enqueue/start/finalize/status scripts, status.json, Codex backend lifecycle integration, and lightweight memory/playbooks. Validation passed for Python syntax, JSON parseability, restricted-PATH Codex dry-run, and a representative enqueue -> start -> finalize -> status lifecycle.

items.title: Build Lyra v2 true-agent foundation
items.detail: Completed on 23 May: Lyra now has a true-agent foundation with identity/factual rules, queue/inbox structure, lifecycle scripts, status output, result/report packaging, memory/playbooks, and current poster-a4 lead-gen integration including supplied-image support.

items.title: Improve Altair lifecycle closure and run hygiene
items.detail: Completed on 23 May: Altair improved its own lifecycle closure behavior. Valid result reports now map to final lifecycle states more reliably, runner completion attempts automatic finalization, status refresh avoids false idle states while real active work remains, and task-lifecycle docs were updated to reflect the safer behavior.

items.title: Upgrade Mission Control for live minor agent activity states
items.detail: Completed on 23 May: Mission Control now reflects richer live status states for Altair/Lyra without page refresh, including current step/detail, freshness, and 1-second updates. Gustav support is present via local status helper, with full automatic conversational microstate instrumentation still limited by deeper runtime hooks.

items.title: Clear the draft-review backlog and turn approved items into scheduled content
items.detail: Buffer itself is healthy, but the content pipeline is empty. The fresh 3 June diagnostic refresh at 18:00 BST succeeded with login OK, schedule page OK, no stuck/failed evidence, and `automation/logs/buffer-health-latest.json` now shows `queuePosts: 0` and `draftPosts: 0`. At the same time, `drafts/review-tracker.md` still shows 25 substantive items awaiting Aaron review, so approvals remain the real bottleneck before anything can be loaded into the scheduling queue. A new helper draft now exists at `drafts/content-approval-priority-shortlist-2026-06-04.md` recommending the first five approvals to speed up that decision.

items.title: Verify repaired AI cron jobs on next scheduled runs
items.detail: This was re-audited live on 2026-06-03 around 21:20 BST. Stored auth records looked superficially healthy, but real isolated cron probes proved the current working path is `openai-codex/gpt-5.4`, not Anthropic: a no-delivery OpenAI probe returned `OK`, while the equivalent `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` probe failed immediately with an `auth_permanent` provider error. Morning Brief and Daily Activity Log Tidy had been failing because they were pinned to Anthropic; Daily Income Research still showed an earlier 04:00 BST preflight error where `payload.model` had been `default`, but that stale issue was already superseded by the later provider audit. All three broken AI cron jobs were patched back onto explicit `openai-codex/gpt-5.4` on 2026-06-03. Current state: repair applied; awaiting the next scheduled runs to confirm end-to-end recovery.
